newsitem.title: UK: LME copper, others cruise up by close.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, others cruise up by close.

text.p: Copper prices bounced smartly after a weak start on Monday, setting the pace for the rest of the metals on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
"After New York came in there was some fresh fund and commission house buying," a trader said. "And the selling dried up at the lower levels in the morning."
Other beneficiaries of the buying interest were zinc, which hit a fresh 23-month high, and aluminium, he added.
Benchmark three-months copper ended the afternoon kerb at $2,270 per tonne, up $22 from Friday.

Copper was still consolidating above $2,230 support after recent strong gains, but eventually prices would likely re-challenge the key $2,290 resistance level, which has stalled rallies twice in the past week.
Near term direction was dependent on Tuesday's LME stocks, expected by some traders to rise by 6,000-7,000 tonnes.
Several traders suggested around 3,000 tonnes of material could be arriving in LME warehouses in Hamburg while 2,000-3,000 tonnes were expected in U.S. LME warehouses.
The recent builds in copper stocks largely reflected strong nearby backwardations that have prevailed in the market recently.

The widening cash to three months backwardation, prompted by tight upcoming dates in late January and early Feburary, was also boosting prices, traders said. Cash/threes ended the day some $15 wider at a $235 backwardation.
One trader said he expected stocks to continue to flow into LME warehouses, roughly estimating some 20,000 tonnes in the next several weeks.
Zinc charged to a fresh 23-month high of $1,153 per tonne. It ended at $1,150, up $13 from Friday.
Aluminium also made upside progress from an indifferent start to the day, finishing the kerb $17 stronger at $1,624.
But it failed to hurdle stiff resistance around $1,625 for the fourth time in a week.
Following the trend, lead ended near the day's highs at $724.50, up $8.50.
Tin, however, was unchanged at $6,050 and nickel was just $10 lower at $7,350.
Alloy ended the kerb $17 stronger at $1525.
